To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cancer patients are at a modestly elevated risk for new primary neoplasia at many sites, including concordant (e.g. upper aerodigestives tract, skin, nervous and endocrine systems) and discordant sites (e.g. breast, kidney and urinary tract).

cancer patients are at a modestly but significantly increased risk for new malignant neoplasia after cancers at several sites, and that the relative risk varies with the site of the first cancer and is highest after cancers of the upper aerodegistive tract, colon and breast.
cancer patients were at increased risk for a subsequent cancer after cancers of the upper aerodegestive tract, colon and rectum, female breast, other female genital organs and testis in males.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the development of a cancer cancer.
the development of new and more efficient methods of analysis for the study of cancer.
the development and application of methods for the analysis of data from cancer registries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cancer patients have a significantly increased risk for new cancers at many sites compared with the general population.
patients with cancer are at an increased risk for a new primary cancer at many sites, but that the risk varies greatly by site, sex, age and time since the first cancer.
the risk for a second primary cancer is elevated after most cancers, with some exceptions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cancer patients have a modestly increased overall risk of new primary cancer, but the risk is high for some specific cancers, especially for cancers of the upper aerodegestive tract, nose and squamous cell skin.
cancer patients are at a moderately increased risk for a new primary cancer, and that the risk is higher for subsequent neoplasia at the same site than at a different site.
cancer patients are at an increased risk for new cancer at many sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer patients are at a modestly higher risk for new primary neoplasm after cancer at many sites.
cancer survivors have a significantly increased risk of new primary cancers at many sites.
cancer patients should be aware of the increased risk for new cancer, especially at sites where SIRs are very high.
